content: Weight and height percentiles are calculated using growth charts and body mass index (BMI) charts. These tools allow for the comparison of a child’s measurements with those of other children in the same age group. By utilizing these percentiles, healthcare providers can monitor a child’s growth over time and assess how their growth compares to that of their peers. Separate growth charts are used for boys and girls because their growth rates and patterns differ. Additionally, there are two distinct sets of charts for each gender: one set is designed for infants aged 0 to 36 months, and the other is for children aged 2 to 20 years. Children who are diagnosed with failure to thrive typically have a weight that falls below the 3rd or 5th percentile for their age. They may also exhibit a declining growth velocity, meaning they are not gaining weight as expected. Furthermore, these children may show a downward shift in their growth percentiles, crossing two or more percentile lines on their growth charts. It has recently been recognized that the current growth charts for infants under 24 months tend to overestimate the expected weight of babies. This overestimation can contribute to the development of obesity in children. The original growth charts, created in 1977, were based on data from middle-class white American infants in Ohio who were fed high-protein bottle-fed diets. In 2006, the World Health Organization revised these growth targets to better reflect a healthier weight standard.
